title: Lifting compatible sections along a finite surjective morphism
statement: Let $f:X\prime\to X$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and let $G$ be a sheaf of sets on the small étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Put $D=X\prime\times_X X\prime$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the section pullbacks and inverse-image composition isomorphisms $c$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. For every $s\prime\in(f^{-1}G)(X\prime)$, the equality $c_{f,p_1,G}(p_1^*s\prime)=c_{f,p_2,G}(p_2^*s\prime)$ (after the canonical identification $f\circ p_1=f\circ p_2$) implies there is $s\in G(X)$ with $f^*s=s\prime$. No uniqueness is asserted by this statement.

proof.text: *$f_1$ is finite.* By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a), applied to the finite $f$ and the base change along $f$, the projection $p_1:X''=X'\times_XX'\to X'$ is finite; by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], $f_1=f\circ p_1$ is finite.

source.place: Lemma 09Z2, statement: '$f_n:X_n\to Y$' (finite, used in the proof through Proposition 03QP)

proof.text: *The sheaves and maps (Stacks: 'for each of the projections $d_j$ there is a map $d_j^{-1}f_n^{-1}\mathcal F\to f_{n+1}^{-1}\mathcal F$. These maps induce maps $\delta_j$').* Put $A=f_*f^{-1}G$ and $B=f_{1*}f_1^{-1}G$, sheaves of sets on $X_{\Et}$ with $A(U)=(f^{-1}G)(U\times_XX')$ and $B(U)=(f_1^{-1}G)(U\times_XX'')$ for $U$ in $X_{\Et}$ (the direct image $(e_*H)(U)=H(U\times_ST)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]). Let $\eta:G\to A$ be the unit, $\eta_U(a)=f^*a$. For $j=1,2$ let $\tau_{j,U}:U\times_XX''\xrightarrow{\sim}(U\times_XX')\times_{X',p_j}X''$ be the canonical isomorphism over $X''$ [def-pc-fibre-product] (sending a point $(u,x'')$ to $((u,p_jx''),x'')$), natural in $U$, and define $\delta_{j,U}:A(U)\to B(U)$ by $\delta_{j,U}(s)=(f_1^{-1}G)(\tau_{j,U})\bigl(c_{f,p_j,G}(p_j^*s)\bigr)$, where $p_j^*s\in(p_j^{-1}f^{-1}G)((U\times_XX')\times_{X'}X'')$ and $c_{f,p_j,G}:p_j^{-1}f^{-1}G\to(f\circ p_j)^{-1}G=f_1^{-1}G$. By clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] ($p_j^*$ commutes with restriction along $U'\times_XX'\to U\times_XX'$, and $c_{f,p_j,G}$ is a morphism of sheaves) and the naturality of $\tau_{j,U}$ in $U$, the $\delta_{j,U}$ commute with restrictions, so $\delta_1,\delta_2:A\to B$ are morphisms of sheaves. For $U=X$, under the identifications of the statement, $\eta_X(s)=f^*s$ and $\delta_{j,X}(s')=c_{f,p_j,G}(p_j^*s')$, so the claim is that $\eta_X$ is a bijection of $G(X)$ onto $\{s'\in A(X):\delta_{1,X}(s')=\delta_{2,X}(s')\}$.

source.place: Lemma 09Z2, proof, second paragraph ('there is a map $d_j^{-1}f_n^{-1}\mathcal F\to f_{n+1}^{-1}\mathcal F$ ... maps $\delta_j$'; 'the canonical map $\mathcal F\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal F$'), for $n=0$ and sheaves of sets as in Remark 09Z3

proof.text: *$\eta$ lands in the equalizer.* Let $E\subseteq A$ be the subpresheaf $E(U)=\{s\in A(U):\delta_{1,U}(s)=\delta_{2,U}(s)\}$ with inclusion $\iota:E\to A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] (1), for the site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and the diagram $A\rightrightarrows B$, $E$ is a sheaf of sets and $\iota$ is an equalizer of $\delta_1,\delta_2$ in the category of sheaves of sets. For $a\in G(U)$, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] (for $g=p_j$, with $(U\times_XX')\times_{X'}X''$ identified with $U\times_XX''$ by $\tau_{j,U}$) gives $\delta_{j,U}(\eta_U(a))=(f_1^{-1}G)(\tau_{j,U})(c_{f,p_j,G}(p_j^*(f^*a)))=(f\circ p_j)^*a=f_1^*a$ for $j=1,2$. So $\delta_1\eta=\delta_2\eta$ and $\eta=\iota\circ\psi$ for a unique morphism of sheaves $\psi:G\to E$, $\psi_U(a)=\eta_U(a)$. It remains to show that $\psi$ is an isomorphism: then $\psi_X$ is a bijection $G(X)\to E(X)$, which is the claim of step 2.

source.place: Remark 09Z3: 'by showing that the sheaf $\mathcal G$ is the equalizer of the two maps $f_{0,*}f_0^{-1}\mathcal G\to f_{1,*}f_1^{-1}\mathcal G$'

proof.text: *Geometric points over $\bar x$.* Fix a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $P$ be the set of geometric points $\bar x':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X'$ with $f\circ\bar x'=\bar x$ and $P_1$ the set of $\bar x'':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X''$ with $f_1\circ\bar x''=\bar x$. By the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], $\bar x''\mapsto(p_1\circ\bar x'',p_2\circ\bar x'')$ is a bijection $P_1\to P\times P$ (a pair $(\bar x'_1,\bar x'_2)\in P\times P$ satisfies $f\bar x'_1=\bar x=f\bar x'_2$, so it is $(p_1,p_2)\circ(\bar x'_1,\bar x'_2)$ for exactly one $(\bar x'_1,\bar x'_2):\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X''$). Since $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] there is $x'\in X'$ over the point $x$ under $\bar x$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-geometric-point-lift] gives $\bar x'\in P$ over $x'$; so $P\neq\emptyset$.

source.place: Lemma 09Z2, proof, third paragraph: 'Let $E=\{\overline x:\Spec(k)\to X\mid f(\overline x)=\overline y\}$. Then $E$ is a finite nonempty set', and the identification of the geometric points of $X_1$ over $\overline y$ with $E^2$ in '$\bigoplus_{e\in E^{n+1}}$'

proof.text: *The stalks of $A$ and $B$ (Stacks: '$(\mathcal F_n)_{\bar y}=\bigoplus_{e\in E^{n+1}}\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ by Proposition 03QP and Lemma 03Q1').* Stalks and germs are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For $\bar x'\in P$ let $r_{\bar x'}:A_{\bar x}\to(f^{-1}G)_{\bar x'}$ be the restriction of germs of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-finite-pushforward-stalk] (for $f$ and $H=f^{-1}G$), and for $\bar x''\in P_1$ let $r^1_{\bar x''}:B_{\bar x}\to(f_1^{-1}G)_{\bar x''}$ be the same for the finite $f_1$ (step 1) and $H=f_1^{-1}G$; by that node $(r_{\bar x'})_{\bar x'}:A_{\bar x}\to\prod_P(f^{-1}G)_{\bar x'}$ and $(r^1_{\bar x''})_{\bar x''}:B_{\bar x}\to\prod_{P_1}(f_1^{-1}G)_{\bar x''}$ are bijective. Let $c_{f,\bar x'}=c_{f,\bar x',G}:(f^{-1}G)_{\bar x'}\to G_{\bar x}$ and $c_{f_1,\bar x''}=c_{f_1,\bar x'',G}:(f_1^{-1}G)_{\bar x''}\to G_{\bar x}$ be the bijections of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. Then $\Phi=(c_{f,\bar x'}\circ r_{\bar x'})_{\bar x'\in P}:A_{\bar x}\to\prod_PG_{\bar x}$ and $\Phi_1=(c_{f_1,\bar x''}\circ r^1_{\bar x''})_{\bar x''\in P_1}:B_{\bar x}\to\prod_{P_1}G_{\bar x}$ are bijective.

source.place: Lemma 09Z2, proof, third paragraph: 'by Proposition 03QP and Lemma 03Q1' (Proposition 03QP (1), the product form for sheaves of sets; Lemma 03Q1 (3))

proof.text: *$\eta$ on stalks is the diagonal.* Let $\eta_{\bar x}:G_{\bar x}\to A_{\bar x}$ be the induced map of stalks (germ of $a\in G(U)$ at $(U,\bar u)$ $\mapsto$ germ of $\eta_U(a)$ at $(U,\bar u)$; well defined since $\eta$ commutes with restrictions, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]). For $\bar x'\in P$: $r_{\bar x'}$ sends the germ of $\eta_U(a)=f^*a$ at $(U,\bar u)$ to its germ at $(U\times_XX',(\bar u,\bar x'))$, and $c_{f,\bar x'}$ sends that to the germ of $a$ at $(U,\bar u)$ by the germ formula of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. Since every element of the colimit of sets $G_{\bar x}$ is the germ of some $a\in G(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], $\Phi\circ\eta_{\bar x}$ is the diagonal $\Delta:G_{\bar x}\to\prod_PG_{\bar x}$, $g\mapsto(g)_{\bar x'\in P}$.

source.place: Lemma 09Z2, proof, last paragraph: 'Here the first map is the diagonal map' (left implicit in the source: that the identification of the stalks carries the augmentation to the diagonal)

proof.text: *Compatibility of $c_{f,p_j,G}$ with the stalk bijections.* Let $\bar x''\in P_1$, $j\in\{1,2\}$ and $\bar x'_j=p_j\circ\bar x''\in P$. For a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar x'_j$ in $X'$, the pair $(W\times_{X',p_j}X'',(\bar w,\bar x''))$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar x''$; for $t\in(f^{-1}G)(W)$ put $L(\text{germ of }t\text{ at }(W,\bar w))=c_{f_1,\bar x''}\bigl(\text{germ of }c_{f,p_j,G}(p_j^*t)\text{ at }(W\times_{X'}X'',(\bar w,\bar x''))\bigr)$. This defines a map $L:(f^{-1}G)_{\bar x'_j}\to G_{\bar x}$: the right side is compatible with the transition maps, since $p_j^*$ commutes with restriction (clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]), $c_{f,p_j,G}$ is a morphism of sheaves, and a morphism $(W_1,\bar w_1)\to(W_2,\bar w_2)$ of pointed neighbourhoods induces one of the base-changed neighbourhoods, so the universal property of the colimit applies [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Claim: $L=c_{f,\bar x'_j}$. Every element of $(f^{-1}G)_{\bar x'_j}$ is the germ of $f^*a$ at $(U\times_XX',(\bar u,\bar x'_j))$ for some pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar x$ and $a\in G(U)$: indeed $c_{f,\bar x'_j}$ is bijective, every element of $G_{\bar x}$ is a germ $[a]_{(U,\bar u)}$, and $c_{f,\bar x'_j}$ maps the germ of $f^*a$ to $[a]_{(U,\bar u)}$ ([lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ]). On such an element, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] (for $g=p_j$) gives $c_{f,p_j,G}(p_j^*f^*a)=f_1^*a$ under $(U\times_XX')\times_{X'}X''\cong U\times_XX''$, which carries $((\bar u,\bar x'_j),\bar x'')$ to $(\bar u,\bar x'')$; so $L$ of it is $c_{f_1,\bar x''}(\text{germ of }f_1^*a\text{ at }(U\times_XX'',(\bar u,\bar x'')))=[a]_{(U,\bar u)}$ by the germ formula for $f_1$, which is $c_{f,\bar x'_j}$ of the same element. Hence $L=c_{f,\bar x'_j}$.

source.place: Lemma 09Z2, proof, last paragraph: 'the map $\bigoplus_{e\in E^{n+1}}M\to\bigoplus_{e\in E^{n+2}}M$ is ... induced by the $(n+2)$ projections $E^{n+2}\to E^{n+1}$' (left implicit in the source: that the identification of the stalks carries $\delta_j$ to the map induced by the $j$-th projection; this step and the next write it out)

proof.text: *$\delta_j$ on stalks is induced by the $j$-th projection.* Let $\delta_{j,\bar x}:A_{\bar x}\to B_{\bar x}$ be the induced map of stalks. Let $\alpha\in A_{\bar x}$ be the germ at $(V,\bar v)$ of $s\in A(V)=(f^{-1}G)(V\times_XX')$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For $\bar x''\in P_1$ with $\bar x'_j=p_j\bar x''$, $r^1_{\bar x''}(\delta_{j,\bar x}(\alpha))$ is the germ of $\delta_{j,V}(s)=(f_1^{-1}G)(\tau_{j,V})(c_{f,p_j,G}(p_j^*s))$ at $(V\times_XX'',(\bar v,\bar x''))$, which equals the germ of $c_{f,p_j,G}(p_j^*s)$ at $((V\times_XX')\times_{X'}X'',((\bar v,\bar x'_j),\bar x''))$ since $\tau_{j,V}$ is an isomorphism of pointed neighbourhoods [def-pc-fibre-product]. Applying $c_{f_1,\bar x''}$ and step 7 (with $W=V\times_XX'$, $\bar w=(\bar v,\bar x'_j)$, $t=s$): $c_{f_1,\bar x''}r^1_{\bar x''}\delta_{j,\bar x}(\alpha)=c_{f,\bar x'_j}(\text{germ of }s\text{ at }(V\times_XX',(\bar v,\bar x'_j)))=c_{f,\bar x'_j}r_{\bar x'_j}(\alpha)$. So the $\bar x''$-component of $\Phi_1\delta_{j,\bar x}(\alpha)$ is the $p_j\bar x''$-component of $\Phi(\alpha)$.

source.place: Lemma 09Z2, proof, last paragraph (the maps induced by the projections), for $n=0$

proof.text: *$\psi$ is bijective on stalks (Stacks: 'it suffices to check on stalks at geometric points ... given an abelian group $M$ the sequence ... is exact', here for sets).* By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-stalk-finite-limits] (equalizer $\iota:E\to A$ of $\delta_1,\delta_2$, step 3), $\iota_{\bar x}:E_{\bar x}\to A_{\bar x}$ is injective with image $\{\alpha:\delta_{1,\bar x}(\alpha)=\delta_{2,\bar x}(\alpha)\}$. Since $\Phi_1$ is injective (step 5), by step 8 and step 4 ($P_1\cong P\times P$) $\delta_{1,\bar x}(\alpha)=\delta_{2,\bar x}(\alpha)$ iff $\Phi(\alpha)_{\bar x'_1}=\Phi(\alpha)_{\bar x'_2}$ for all $\bar x'_1,\bar x'_2\in P$, i.e. iff $\Phi(\alpha)$ is a constant family, i.e. (as $P\neq\emptyset$, step 4) iff $\Phi(\alpha)\in\Delta(G_{\bar x})$. From $\eta=\iota\psi$ we get $\eta_{\bar x}=\iota_{\bar x}\psi_{\bar x}$, so $\Phi\iota_{\bar x}\psi_{\bar x}=\Delta$ (step 6). $\Delta$ is injective since $P\neq\emptyset$, hence $\psi_{\bar x}$ is injective. For $\epsilon\in E_{\bar x}$, $\Phi(\iota_{\bar x}\epsilon)=\Delta(g)$ for some $g$, so $\Phi\iota_{\bar x}(\psi_{\bar x}g)=\Phi\iota_{\bar x}(\epsilon)$ and, $\Phi$ and $\iota_{\bar x}$ being injective, $\psi_{\bar x}(g)=\epsilon$. So $\psi_{\bar x}$ is bijective.

source.place: Lemma 09Z2, proof, third and last paragraphs (check on stalks; the sequence for a set $M$ and the nonempty finite set $E$), as transposed to sets by Remark 09Z3

proof.text: *Conclusion.* For every point $x\in X$ choose an algebraic closure $\Omega_x$ of $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $\bar x_x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_x\to X$ be the geometric point given by $x$ and $\kappa(x)\to\Omega_x$ [def-weil-geometric-point]; these geometric points cover $X$. By step 9 every $\psi_{\bar x_x}$ is bijective, so by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] $\psi:G\to E$ is an isomorphism; in particular $\psi_X:G(X)\to E(X)$, $s\mapsto f^*s$, is bijective, which by steps 2 and 3 is the statement.

source.place: Lemma 09Z2, proof, third paragraph ('it suffices to check on stalks at geometric points (Theorem 03PU)'), for sheaves of sets; Remark 09Z3 (global sections of the equalizer)

lean.statement:
theorem finiteSurjectiveSetDescent_compatible_lift
    {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X) [IsFinite f] [Surjective f]
    (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))) :
    ∀ s' : ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback f).obj G).obj.obj
          (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ f).obj
            (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)))),
        etaleSetDescentComparison f (pullback.fst f f) G (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) s' =
          eqToHom (congrArg
            (fun k : pullback f f ⟶ X ↦ ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback k).obj G).obj.obj
              (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ k).obj
                (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))))) (pullback.condition (f := f) (g := f)).symm)
            (etaleSetDescentComparison f (pullback.snd f f) G
              (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) s') →
          ∃ s : G.obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))),
            etaleSetDescentUnit f G (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) s = s'
